title: Cap. IX: Heb. 7:9–10 called to examine immediate imputation
pass_a_gloss: Chapter IX opens. Its declared task is to call to examination the doctrine of the imputation of the first sin from Hebrews 7:9–10 on Levi being tithed in Abraham's loins. Head I: Placeus judges it already plain that the doctrine of antecedent or immediate imputation of the first sin rests on no Scriptural foundations. The remaining question is whether that doctrine can at least be illustrated — for it certainly cannot be proved — from Hebrews 7:9–10, where Levi is said to have been tithed in Abraham's loins; Placeus will look briefly. Opponent D. Garissoles (D. G., margin Cap. x. §1) says it is customary for theologians to declare from this locus the nature and reason of original sin passing into us from Adam. Placeus praises the phrase original sin: Garissoles is naming writers who not only fail to teach immediate imputation but openly condemn it. Placeus could produce many passages from Augustine, Bucer, Martyr, Gualther, Gerhard, and others; but lest he seem longer than fair in a clear matter, he will be content with Anselm's words alone.
pass_b_english:
CAPUT IX. The doctrine of the imputation of the first sin is called to examination from Hebrews 7:9–10, on Levi being tithed in Abraham's loins.

I. That the doctrine of antecedent or immediate imputation of the first sin rests on no foundations in Scripture is already, I think, plain. Can it at least be illustrated — for it certainly cannot be proved — from Hebrews 7:9–10, where Levi is said to have been tithed in Abraham's loins? Let us see in a few words. D. Garissoles says it is customary for theologians to declare from this place the nature and reason of original sin as it passes into us from Adam. He said well, "of original sin": for he names certain writers who not only do not teach immediate imputation, but openly condemn it. I could bring forward many places from Augustine, Bucer, Martyr, Gualther, Gerhard, and others; but lest I seem longer than is fair in a clear matter, I will be content with these words of Anselm alone.
source_text: CAPVT IX. Declaratio doctrinae de Imputatione primi peccati, Ex Hebr. cap. 7. verf. 9. 10. de decimatione Levi in lumbis Abrahae, vocatur ad examen. I. Doctrinam de imputatione primi peccati antecedente seu immediata nullis Scripturae fundamentis innixam esse jam, opinor, patet. Num ea saltem illustrari possit, nam probari certe non potest, ex Hebr. vii. 9. 10. ubi dicitur Levi decimatus in lumbis Abrahae, paucis videamus. Ait D. G. Originalis peccati in nos ex Adamo transeuntis naturam & rationem ex hoc loco declarare Theologis solemne esse. Bene dixit originalis peccati: Nominat enim quosdam qui imputationem immediatam non modo non docent, sed aperte damnant. Possem ex Augustino, Bucero, Martyre, Gualtero, Gerhardo, &c. multa loca proferre: sed ne in re clara aequo longior videar, unius Anselmi his verbis ero contentus.

choices.decision: Heb 7 may illustrate at most; cannot prove immediate imputation
Garissoles's own wording names condemners of immediate imputation
